Date: 2028-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity intake: telemetry slices, slotting & GPU mapping

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team loved Redwood's deterministic latency options. We're preparing to scope a reserved/dedicated capacity commitment for PlanetCart's checkout recommender and conversational support feature. Before we can commit internally, the infra and finance teams asked for a short pre-sales sizing worksheet focused on:

- daily and peak concurrency (concurrent sessions + queries per second)
- prompt / completion token distributions (percentiles)
- session durations and KV cache reuse expectations
- traffic seasonality (day/hour/week) and burst windows
- any recommended GPU SKU mapping for an initial pilot (8-week) and scale plan

I've attached a small sample export (planetcart-traffic-sample.csv) and a one-page prompt mix that shows our estimated 70/30 split between short assist queries and longer generation flows. Can you send a lightweight questionnaire we can fill, or tell us the exact telemetry slices you need?

We aim to have a preliminary sizing by next Tuesday so procurement can start the contracting timeline.

Best,
Alex Torres
VP Engineering — PlanetCart
atorres@planetcart.com

Alex — great to hear, thanks for the sample. Attaching a short checklist below to speed things up. If you can drop the CSV and prompt-mix answers into the fields we can produce a pilot footprint (GPU SKUs, slotting strategy, expected p99 latency and cost estimate) within 48 hours.

Quick questionnaire (please paste / attach values):
1) Traffic windows: typical daily active hours and two representative peak hours (local timezone)
2) Baseline QPS and peak QPS (1-min and 5-min peaks) for each workload: recommender / conv-support
3) Concurrent sessions and average queries per session (mean and 95th pct)
4) Prompt token distribution: median, p90, p99 for prompts and completions (tokens)
5) % of requests that are embeddings or rerank vs text-gen
6) Session duration distribution and average KV reuse (cache hit rate)
7) Target p99 latency SLO for the pilot and for steady state
8) Expected sustained pilot throughput (RPS) and burst tolerance (seconds)
9) Any preference for GPU family (A100, H100, L4e) or strict PCIe availability
10) Compliance / data residency constraints we should account for

Notes / definitions:
- For sizing we prefer per-minute QPS and 95th/99th percentile concurrent sessions rather than monthly averages — helps sizing for slotting and preemptible strategies.
- If you can provide even a day of representative telemetry in CSV with timestamps, prompt_len, completion_len, session_id, model_type it is ideal.

I'll loop Marissa (capacity planning) and Karthik (runtime tuning) on any follow-ups.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — pasted answers inline and attached the full day export; see prompt-mix-summary.xlsx for breakdown.

1) Traffic windows: 06:00–22:00 PT, peak hours 09:00–10:00 and 19:00–19:30 PT
2) Baseline QPS: recommender 40 QPS, conv-support 25 QPS; 1-min peak: recommender 220 QPS, conv-support 140 QPS; 5-min peak smoothing: recommender 150 QPS, conv-support 90 QPS
3) Concurrent sessions: recommender mean 120, p95 820; conv-support mean 60, p95 420
4) Prompt token distribution (prompts/completions): median 15/35, p90 60/120, p99 220/800
5) % embeddings/rerank: 10% embeddings, 5% rerank, 85% text-gen
6) Session duration: median 18s, mean 42s; KV cache hit: estimated 68% (mostly chat context reuse)
7) Target p99 latency: pilot 450ms for short prompts, steady state 300ms for short prompts (we can tolerate higher for long generations)
8) Pilot sustained throughput: target 300 RPS (combined), burst tolerance: 30s at 2.5x sustained
9) No strict GPU family preference; we prefer lower cost H100 if quantization works; otherwise A100 mix is OK
10) Data residency: US only; SOC2 evidence will be required at contracting

Attachment: prompt-mix-summary.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB), planetcart-traffic-sample.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

Alex / Sean — quick follow-up from capacity planning: a few clarifying items before we size the pilot footprint. Answers below in-line.

1) For the burst tolerance (30s at 2.5x) — is that simultaneous across both workloads, or per-workload? If simultaneous, we size for combined 2.5x.
   - Alex: please confirm (if simultaneous we'll plan for an upper bound with pre-warmed slots).
2) KV cache reuse: is the 68% estimate across sessions, or only for conv-support where session affinity exists? If it's mostly conv-support, we can prioritize session-pinning.
   - Alex: any breakdown by workload would help (estimated conv-support hit 82%, recommender hit 20%).
3) Prompt p99 long completions (800 tokens) — are those rare analytics jobs or do they occur during user-visible flows? If they are user-visible we recommend reserving a small pool of larger-memory GPUs or allowing fallback to mixed-precision/quantized variants to avoid tail blow-ups.

Sizing notes / next steps we will deliver:
- Pilot SKU map (recommended: 4 x H100-equivalent for slotting + 1 heavy-memory A100 for long-completion fallback)
- Slotting strategy: dedicated hot slots for conversational affinity + elastic shared slots for recommender (to improve utilization)
- Expected p99 estimate: ~420–480ms for short prompts on a 4x H100 pilot (depends on batching behavior)
- Cost ballpark: we'll send a pilot monthly commit estimate in the next email once Alex confirms burst simultaneity and KV split

If you can confirm the two quick points above we'll finalize the SKU map and cost. Thanks!

—Marissa
